§11.2.7 Maps and Treemaps

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

charts-maps-and-treemaps · charts types

✅ Normative

A treemap MUST be rendered with one row per tile: the tile's label and its printed value. Tile area MUST NOT be turned into a value: no axis calibrates it. A map with printed values per region MUST be rendered with one row per printed region–value pair. A shading-only map with a discrete legend MUST give each region whose fill matches one swatch unambiguously that legend class, copied verbatim.

Treemaps

A tile's printed value is copied as printed. A tile that prints no value, only a comparator (<1%), or a truncated label (Re…) gets no estimated value: its printed text is kept as it is, and nothing is read from its area.

✅ Sample — threat-report-2025_p29

Every tile prints its label and share: eight rows in reading order, left to right and top to bottom. The percent sign is printed raised beside each number and is written as a superscript. All tile text is set in a heavier weight.

Maps

Two readable layers, each with its own place in the table (see also Geographic Maps§12.2.4):

  • Values printed per region or per pin — one row per printed pair: the region or callout text as the label, the printed value copied as printed. A callout on a leader line (DE 1) is read like any other.
  • Shading with a discrete legend — each region's fill is compared with the legend swatches, and the region takes the legend class verbatim. A region whose fill falls between two adjacent swatches is given no class.

Where a map's classes go. A choropleth MUST be one table with one row per region, in reading order: the region label, its printed value when it has one, and its legend class in a last column headed by the legend's printed title (no header row when the legend has none). A region with an ambiguous fill has an empty class cell. Where the region names are recognised from the outlines rather than printed, the region column's header carries data-recognised — see Geographic Maps§12.2.4.

A checker judges a class on meaning: it accepts the class string, an equivalent range, or a value inside the class's range, and treats region-name variants (CO / Colorado) as the same region.

✅ Sample — apport_p19


Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Apportionment of the U.S. House of Representatives Based on the 2020 Census (public domain)

Both layers on one page: every state prints its seat count, and the fill classes its change, so each state's row holds both — 50 states. Five states are shown, then the rest; the DE 1 callout on a leader line is read like any other. Delaware's fill is too small to compare with the swatches, so its class cell is empty. The agency footer is elided.

✅ Sample — cdc_p3


Source: U.S. CDC, Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (public domain)

No values anywhere — state abbreviations printed, six legend classes, no legend title. Each region takes its class: every state, DC and territory shown (about 53 regions). Four regions spread across the classes are shown, then the rest. The legend draws ≥35% as a > glyph over an underline bar; ≥35% is the reading, and a checker treats >35% as the same class. The source lines are cut off at the page edge and are elided.

❌ Counter-sample — regional-catastrophe-report-2023_p54

Event pins over a regional map, each callout naming an event and describing its losses (Eco: USD1.9bn / Ins: USD240mn). The map's shading has no discrete legend to class regions against, and a pin's position is not a value, so the map gives no chart table: its printed text is transcribed as text. The data of this page is the loss chart beside the map, which is a chart table like any other; its bars print no values, so they are estimates on the 20-unit grid. The map's title, callouts and place names are elided.
